facts.fact: Masr Times reports that the communications ministry, through NTRA, launched the 'Digital Identity' biometric verification system, which matches a face and biometric data to Civil Status Authority records and is being applied on a pilot, gradual basis.
Masr Times reports the verification infrastructure is open to the four licensed mobile operators and integrates licensed e-signature firms, with services varying by operator during the pilot.

EGY.note: Nothing on civil register and ID links.

facts.fact: Masr Times reports a digital infrastructure, in pilot, links the communications ministry bodies, the Civil Status Authority, mobile operators and e-signature firms to verify identity and exchange data.

EGY.note: No data protection law is named; only a general reference to data protection requirements.

facts.fact: Masr Times states that an electronic signature made through the system has legal force under the rules regulating electronic signature, with licensed e-signature companies issuing the certificates.

EGY.note: The services are mobile operators' services, not government services.
No count of people holding a national ID.
Nothing on a number at birth.
Nothing on who operates the national ID system.
Only operators' checks against civil status data, which is not a public register keyed on the number.
Civil Status records are matched but the ID system itself is not described.

facts.fact: Masr Times reports that mobile line purchase and activation and e-wallet opening are being checked by biometric match against Civil Status Authority records, in a pilot with the four licensed operators.
